headline: Congress Weighs Stricter Social Media Age Limits for Children
seoTitle: Congress Weighs Social Media Age Limits for Children | FMB News
seoDescription: Philippine lawmakers are weighing stricter age limits, parental consent and platform safeguards for minors using social media.
deck: Lawmakers are considering tighter age-based restrictions and platform safeguards as Congress works through competing proposals on minors' social media access.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Philippine lawmakers are pushing tighter restrictions on children's access to social media, including proposals that would bar younger children from maintaining accounts and require stronger safeguards for teenagers.

Pasig Rep. Roman Romulo, who chairs the House technical working group handling child online-safety measures, has been involved in reconciling bills with different age thresholds and requirements. Current House proposals include bans below age 13, below age 15 and below age 16, depending on the bill.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The approved FMB News brief described a Sunday push for an under-13 ban and additional controls for users aged 14 to 17. Independent House records confirm that Congress is actively considering multiple child online-safety measures, but they do not support treating one threshold as enacted law.
The debate intensified after the Zamboanga school shooting, which renewed scrutiny of minors' social-media access, circulation of violent material and platform response times.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Age-assurance rules can affect millions of families and raise questions about privacy, parental consent, platform liability and enforcement. The proposals remain legislative measures and are not yet law.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Congress will have to reconcile competing age thresholds and define how age assurance, parental consent and platform duties would work before a final measure can advance.
